source.title_on_document: The value of generative AI in creative teams depends on when it enters collective search

supplement.where: Supplementary Information is appended to the main text (PDF pp. 19-70, numbered SI pp. 1-52). Processed group-level data and code at https://osf.io/eapdn; AI-rater scoring code 'detailed in the submitted supplementary files' (SI p. 8, PDF p. 26).
supplement.holds: All arm-level statistics: Supplementary Table 1 (arm Ns, creativity means and SDs), Table 5 (planned contrasts, Hedges g, CIs), Tables 6-7 (dimension contrasts), Tables 8-10 (timing models with HC3 SEs), Table 13 (robustness), Tables 15-16 (alpha diversity and proposal count), Table 22 (AI-rated creativity). The main text reports only g and p for the headline contrasts. Tables 32-34 cite 'Extended Data Fig.' 7-10, which appear in this PDF as Supplementary Figures 7-10.

paper_design_summary: In a computer laboratory, 444 participants (logged in by student ID) were randomly formed into 148 three-person teams that completed a 40-minute product-design task in three stages (15 min divergent search, 15 min convergent selection, 10 min final proposal). Sessions were randomized to five AI-access regimes for an integrated DeepSeek V3.2 chat assistant: Stage 1 only (C1), Stage 2 only (C2), all stages (C3), no AI (C4), and Stage 1 with a persistent warning (C5), crossed with three tasks. Four blind experts rated each team's final proposal document; the primary outcome is a calibrated team-level creativity composite.

studies.label: Phase-contingent AI access in three-person teams (product-design task)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Team sessions assigned to one of five AI-access regimes (C1 Stage-1 AI, C2 Stage-2 AI, C3 full-process AI, C4 no AI, C5 Stage-1 AI plus warning) crossed with three product-design tasks; 150 sessions in a fully randomized sequence, teams formed at random and allocated sequentially.
assignment.quote: The sequence of these 150 sessions was fully randomized. Participants were randomly formed into teams of three and then sequentially allocated to a session following this randomized sequence.

participants.exclusions: Analytic sample is 148 teams (444 people): C1 30 teams/90, C2 30/90, C3 30/90, C4 29/87, C5 29/87. 150 sessions were generated; S1.1 says the shortfall was 'due to a system setup error that created an extra C1T1 session and omitted a C1T3 session, as well as the removal of two sessions because of invalid data' (PDF p. 22). Supplementary Table 2 (PDF p. 28) reports 0 exclusions after each sample-flow step, counted from the 148-team analytic file. The number of people randomized is not stated.
participants.who: Participants logged in with a student ID; baseline covariates include grade and discipline. Teams of three; 45 RMB base fee plus up to 50 RMB bonus for the top 10 groups.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly; interface text translated from Chinese, payment in RMB, IRB at Chinese Academy of Sciences

ai_tool.name_model: DeepSeek V3.2 via API, temperature 0.1, assigned a specific role; new session per group
ai_tool.how_used: Integrated chat panel in the team workspace; each member could query the model independently, and team chat was streamed to the AI in real time. The panel was greyed out in stages without access. Teams in AI arms logged 12.48 to 30.00 mean LLM calls (Supplementary Table 1).

task.description: Team product-design task combining two distant objects (T1 backpack + pet accessory, T2 refrigerator + calendar, T3 shoes + map). Each team submitted one final document (product name, feature list, description, 250-word limit) that could hold several proposals.
task.duration: 40 minutes: 15 min divergent search, 15 min convergent selection, 10 min final review and submission

outcomes.name: Human-rated team creativity composite (calibrated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Four experts, blind to condition, scored every proposal; Creativity = 0.70 Originality + 0.15 Appropriateness + 0.15 Elaboration, with Originality = 0.9 Quality + 0.1 Quantity + Naming bonus. Averaged across proposals within a team, then across raters; rater-severity (MFRM-equivalent) calibration. ICC(2,k) = 0.421. Robustness: leave-one-rater-out, expert-only, mixed model, bootstrap (Supplementary Table 13, PDF p. 39); task-specific contrasts (Supplementary Table 14).

outcomes.name: Originality-quality rating ('Quality' in the dimension tables)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of how novel, surprising and non-obvious the product concept is; team mean across proposals and four raters. ICC(2,k) = 0.372.

outcomes.name: Originality composite
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Originality = 0.9 originality-quality rating + 0.1 originality-quantity score (deduplicated count of valid features mapped to a capped 1-7 scale) + naming-novelty bonus (0, 0.5 or 1). ICC(2,k) = 0.404. Timing-model coefficients in Supplementary Tables 9-10.

outcomes.name: Appropriateness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of usefulness, feasibility and plausible user need. ICC(2,k) = 0.349.

outcomes.name: Elaboration
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of detail and development of the proposal (250-word limit). ICC(2,k) = 0.512.

outcomes.name: Text quality (supplementary indicator, not in composite)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rating of whether the text is clearly categorized, readable and logically coherent. ICC(2,k) = 0.384.

outcomes.name: Alpha diversity (semantic breadth within a team's final document)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean pairwise TF-IDF distance among paragraph-level idea units within one team's final proposal document. It measures variety inside one team's output, not similarity across teams, so it is coded flexibility rather than diversity. The paper treats it as a mechanism (process) variable.

outcomes.name: AI-rated creativity (pooled z-score of ten LLM raters)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Ten LLM raters (Claude Opus 4.6/4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V3, DeepSeek V4 pro, Gemini 3.1 flash/pro, GPT 5.5, GPT 5.5 pro, Kimi K2.6) scored the same proposals; team means z-scored and pooled (ai_pool_z_all10). Used as an evaluator diagnostic only, not as an outcome of interest. AI-rated condition contrasts appear only as Hedges g in Supplementary Fig. 10b (figure).

company_involvement.description: None stated. Commercial LLMs serve as the assistant (DeepSeek V3.2) and as diagnostic raters; no company role in funding or authorship is stated. The document has no funding statement.

eligibility.reason: Teams were randomly assigned to generative-AI access regimes, including a no-AI control (C4), on a product-design ideation task (PDF pp. 21-22, S1.1). 444 people in 148 teams were analyzed (Supplementary Table 1, PDF p. 27), well above 50, although assignment and analysis are at the team level (148 teams; 29-30 teams per arm). The primary outcome is expert-rated creativity of each team's final proposal (PDF p. 8; SI pp. 5-6).

one_line_finding: Compared with no AI, Stage-1 (divergent) AI raised expert-rated team creativity (4.86 vs 4.35, g=0.81, p=0.003) and full-process AI did too (g=0.77, p=0.004), while Stage-2-only AI (g=0.25, p=0.328) and warning-framed Stage-1 AI (g=0.43, p=0.104) did not (Supplementary Table 5, PDF p. 31).
open_questions: AI availability during production is partial: C1 and C5 had AI only in Stage 1 and C2 only in Stage 2, while the scored final proposal was written in Stage 3, when only C3 had AI. I coded the outcomes with_ai with ai_available_when_produced = mixed, since AI use and output production are in one 40-minute session; a reviewer may prefer a different code for C1, C2 and C5.
Unit of assignment and analysis is the team (148 teams, 29-30 per arm). Criterion 2 counts 444 people, but participant-level standard deviations do not exist; the outcome SDs are team-level.
Which C1-C5 contrast is primary for pooling: C3 (full-process, closest to free chatbot use) vs C4 or C1 vs C4 (the paper's headline). Rule 3 of the codebook would point to C3 vs C4.
Sample-flow inconsistency: S1.1 says two sessions were removed for invalid data and one C1T3 session was omitted, while Supplementary Table 2 reports 0 exclusions. People randomized is not stated.

Small numeric inconsistencies: Supplementary Fig. 5 caption gives C1-C4 g=0.80, C2-C4 p=0.34, C5-C4 g=0.42, p=0.11, versus g=0.81, p=0.328, g=0.43, p=0.104 in Supplementary Table 5; Supplementary Table 12 gives C5 adjusted mean 4.643 and raw mean 4.653.
notes: Design class lab_rct: the task ran on an 'online' web platform, but S1.3 (PDF p. 22) says the experiment was conducted in a controlled computer laboratory with partitions and internet disabled. No across-people diversity outcome is reported; alpha diversity is within one team's document. Process measures not listed as outcomes because they are not scored on the creative output: Stage-1 chat characters, semantic proximity of proposals to AI outputs (Supplementary Tables 20-22), and AI-human rater divergence (Supplementary Table 26). Dimension-level timing-model coefficients (Supplementary Tables 9-10, PDF pp. 35-36) and task-level contrasts (Supplementary Tables 14 and 28) are not repeated here. The paper states the human-rated creativity score as primary; the preregistration text quoted in the paper names only the conditions and the planned sample, so primary is coded paper_primary rather than preregistered_primary.
